query: For a FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy used as a thin coating on a conventional metal substrate, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation during sliding in the intended high-temperature operating regime? Define a controlled change relative to a baseline coating condition, predict the corresponding directional changes in wear and deformation, state the regime in which those predictions should hold, identify supporting prior evidence, and specify a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: During high-temperature sliding (≈600 °C), overall wear resistance and microscopic deformation of FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy alloy (HEA) coatings are governed by the in-situ formation of a nanocomposite tribo-oxide ‘glaze’ layer that is enriched in Cu and Cr; increasing the nominal Cu concentration in the HEA promotes faster nucleation and higher area fraction of this lubricious Cu-rich oxide, thereby decreasing the steady-state wear rate and subsurface plastic strain.
generation.material_initial_state: Baseline arc-sprayed Fe₀.₂Ni₀.₂Cr₀.₂Co₀.₂Cu₀.₂ (equiatomic) coating, ≈100 µm thick, on hardened AISI 1045 steel, as-sprayed (no post heat treatment).
generation.intervention: Increase the Cu atomic fraction from 0.20 to 0.35 (Fe₀.₁₇Ni₀.₁₇Cr₀.₁₇Co₀.₁₄Cu₀.₃₅), keeping all other deposition parameters unchanged.
generation.conditions: Dry reciprocating sliding against an Al₂O₃ counter-body, 5 N normal load, 5 Hz, 10 mm stroke, temperature 600 ± 10 °C, ambient air, total sliding distance 1 km.
generation.structural_mediator: Thickness, continuity, and chemistry of the tribo-oxide glaze layer (specifically the volume fraction of fine CuOx/Cr₂O₃ phases embedded in a nanocrystalline FCC matrix).
generation.mechanism: Higher Cu supersaturation accelerates segregation of Cu to the sliding surface and promotes the formation of a Cu-rich oxide that is softer and more plastically compliant than the surrounding Cr-rich oxide. This composite glaze lowers the shear stress at the interface, reducing frictional heating and suppressing subsurface dislocation activity, which diminishes wear depth and near-surface plastic strain accumulation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline coating, the 0.35 Cu variant will (a) exhibit ≥30 % lower specific wear rate (mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹) and (b) show ≥25 % reduction in average kernel average misorientation (KAM) within the first 2 µm beneath the wear track, indicating less plastic deformation.
generation.baseline: Specific wear rate of the equiatomic coating at 600 °C is assumed 3 × 10⁻⁵ mm³ N⁻¹ m⁻¹ with average KAM of 1.2° in the subsurface after 1 km sliding.
generation.boundary: Prediction expected to hold for 500–700 °C in dry air, normal loads 2–10 N, and counter-bodies that do not form transfer films (e.g., Al₂O₃ or Si₃N₄). Below 400 °C or in lubricated environments, oxide-glaze formation is limited and the hypothesis may not apply.
generation.uncertainty: Quantitative magnitudes (30 % wear reduction, 25 % KAM decrease) are estimates; actual values may vary with porosity and residual stress of the sprayed coating. No direct prior study on Cu-enriched FeNiCrCoCu at 600 °C was found, so mechanistic inference is based on general knowledge of Cu segregation and oxide-glaze tribology.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two coatings (baseline and Cu-enriched). Perform identical high-temperature sliding tests as specified. Characterize wear tracks by 3D profilometry for wear volume and by EBSD cross-sections for KAM mapping; analyze surface chemistry with XPS or TEM-EDS to quantify Cu/Cr oxide content in the glaze layer.
measurements: Average KAM within 0–2 µm of surface below wear track
Glaze layer thickness and Cu/(Cu+Cr) atomic ratio by TEM-EDS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if (1) the Cu-enriched coating does NOT show at least a 10 % reduction in both specific wear rate and subsurface KAM relative to baseline, OR (2) surface analyses reveal no measurable increase (≤5 at %) in Cu content within the tribo-oxide layer compared with baseline.
